# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: diagnose the single failing val task (8) to root causes, then ship a multi-lever candidate across BOTH surfaces (prompt + tools) rather than one tweak. Two primary, high-certainty root causes identified from the trace: (A) the write was never executed after the user's "yes" (action stall), and (B) the agent enumerated only 4 of 5 reservations and missed the one it needed. Can't yet cite a LEDGER row (first iteration).
- Why multi-lever: reward is DB + COMMUNICATE; only a correct WRITE moves DB. A prose rule alone can't guarantee enumeration completeness, so cluster B got a deterministic loop tool; the action-stall is a behavior the prompt can force (there is no tool that can make the model emit a call), so A got the strongest prompt contract + worked example.
- Plateau/stall: n/a (iteration 1).
- What to try next iteration: if ACCEPTED, re-diagnose on the new trace to confirm book fires and the right flight number (from history) is chosen. If REJECTED, (1) add a composite atomic book-and-confirm write tool for cluster A, and (2) move price computation into an in-body helper / compute tool for cluster D, since prose + docstrings may be insufficient for the mid reader.
